source_reference: No held table (095r: IFS Boileau and Sturrock and RF Inheritance give group levels, not held as files)
caveats: No UK source gives transfers given as a share of the giver wealth by band (095r). Baseline TR = 0 and the sector aggregate cancels
proposed_ruling: remain unset (consequence: cells run with TR = 0 or a labelled scenario the author authorises)
open_question_or_data_request: WAS 7215 gift and inheritance modules; HMRC IHT tables by estate size (not held); ONS request for gifts by band

variable: Estates passing at death by size and composition
definition: Estates passing at death: number, size and composition by estate size
caveats: The held moment is 2007-08 and probate-based; no current estate table is held
open_question_or_data_request: HMRC IHT statistics (tables 12.1 to 12.3 are held as ods in 097r but not parsed for estates by size)

variable: Legacy heir rule (one heir, G = 30 years)
definition: Legacy heir rule: one heir per generation, every G = 30 years, heir taxed on the receipt from zero
source_reference: model_v3/core/kernel.py step_death; plan decisions D6, D20; 094r A4
value_or_range: G = 30 years (a model period, not a UK estimate)
caveats: A legacy mechanism, not a measured transfer rate; judgement
proposed_ruling: remain as the legacy arm only

variable: Two-year top-decile persistence and entry
definition: Two-year top-decile persistence and entry: 80% of families in the top decile stay; about 90% of entrants come from the ninth decile; 7% of the bottom half move to the top half
source_reference: moments.csv AB-02 (Advani, Bangham, Leslie 2021, Fig 13, PDF 22 to 23)
caveats: Family wealth deciles from the paper; base 2014-16 (PDF 4) or 2016-18 (PDF 23); not pack deciles; no full transition matrix
proposed_ruling: ready for implementation as validation moments
open_question_or_data_request: WAS 7215 panel for a decile transition matrix

variable: Four-year rank correlation and same-decile share
definition: Four-year rank correlation and same-decile share of age-adjusted per-adult wealth, individuals aged 25-54, 2016-18 to 2020-22 (low-to-middle and higher income)
source_reference: moments.csv BF-04, BF-06 (Resolution Foundation, Before the fall, Table 1 PDF 45, Fig 22)
value_or_range: rank correlation 74 / 77; same decile 33% / 32%; 27% (aged 25-34) and 34% (35-54) for higher income
caveats: Income groups, age-adjusted deciles, a different population from S20: not spliced with it
proposed_ruling: ready for implementation as validation moments
relation_to_existing_row: supports I-W4c (reported central 75.5 is a J midpoint)

variable: Band-to-band and stage transition matrix
definition: Full band-to-band and stage transition matrix
caveats: No UK matrix is held; only summary measures above
proposed_ruling: further data required (consequence: bands evolve only through the model flows; validation uses S20 and S21)

variable: Age structure of the adult population
definition: Age structure of the adult population (GB, 2024, 2030, 2040 projections)
calculation_and_script: derive_debt_demography.py: single years summed to bands
caveats: Principal projection only; age not stage

variable: Mortality, period qx and survival from 65
definition: Mortality: period qx 2024 by age band; survival from 65; expected adult deaths in 2024
source_reference: ONS ad hoc 3459; demography_age_bands.csv; survival_from_65_period2024.csv; adult_deaths_gb_2024.csv
calculation_and_script: derive_debt_demography.py: expected deaths = population x qx; tolerance 5 deaths on the band sum
caveats: Age and sex only: no wealth gradient (richer people live longer), so deaths by band are not derived; period life table, not a cohort forecast
proposed_ruling: ready for implementation for the age hazard; wealth gradient remain unset
open_question_or_data_request: ONS or WAS-linked mortality by wealth (request)

variable: Working-to-retired transition hazard by band
definition: Working-to-retired transition hazard by band
source_reference: No held table of entry into retirement by band; the State Pension age is an external parameter not held
caveats: An age structure alone does not give an entry hazard without a retirement-age rule and band-specific retirement timing
proposed_ruling: further data required (a labelled scenario on the pension age is possible; author decision)
open_question_or_data_request: WAS 7215 longitudinal status changes; DWP State Pension age schedule

variable: Household formation and dissolution
definition: Household formation and dissolution
caveats: Left out of the first design (096r); changes weights, not the identity

variable: Adults per household by pack band
definition: Adults per household by pack band (household to person weight), R8
source_reference: Table 2.11 and Table 2.13 over Table 2.5; person_household_weights_by_band.csv; adults_per_household_all_rounds.csv
calculation_and_script: derive_bands_stages.py: persons 16+ over households; tolerance 0.0005 on the all-household ratios
caveats: The two published tables give different adult counts (Table 2.13 is 1.858m lower in R8); which is the right adult base is not stated in the held tables; band rows use the decile-aligned GBP groups (S02)
proposed_ruling: implement with a scenario range (Table 2.11 against 2.13)
relation_to_existing_row: supports I-D4h central 1.93; contradicts its low 1.77 (below both tables)

variable: Person weights by stage within band
definition: Person weights by stage within band (household stage mix)
source_reference: none: stage is a person attribute in the held table, household stage is not
caveats: A household has mixed stages; no held table

variable: Audit I-D4a wealth to GDP
definition: I-D4a wealth to GDP (low 5.80, central 5.94, high 7.5)
value_or_range: Central 5.94 reproduces on GDP 2,284bn; on the pack GDP 2,211.48bn it is 6.14; low 5.80 is not reproduced (held NBS S.14 net worth 2021 / 2,284bn = 5.03)
caveats: GDP differs between the register and the pack (3.2%) and is not reconciled in held files; the low is a different basis
proposed_ruling: report the disagreement; no register edit
relation_to_existing_row: supports central, contradicts the low (basis) and the pack GDP
open_question_or_data_request: Which GDP series the register intends

variable: Audit I-D4b, I-D4g, I-D4h adult base and adults per household
definition: I-D4b share of adults at or above W_min; I-D4h adults per household; I-D4c
value_or_range: I-D4b low 49.3 reproduces (households at or above 300,000, labelled adults); high 64.3 lies inside the held household bracket 59.2 to 72.7 (at or above 200,000 to at or above 85,000); central 54.9 (an adult share from a lognormal fit) lies below that bracket and the held tables cannot test it; I-D4h central 1.93 reproduces (1.9282), but Table 2.13 gives 1.8593 and the low 1.77 sits below both
caveats: The 150,000 point lies inside a band, so no held cell gives it; see audit note
relation_to_existing_row: supports I-D4b low and high and I-D4h central; I-D4b central not testable and below the bracket; contradicts I-D4h low
open_question_or_data_request: Which adult base the register intends

variable: Audit I-W5a and I-W5e top-decile and pension shares
definition: I-W5a, I-W5e: top-decile share and pension share (R8)
value_or_range: I-W5a 40.7 reproduces (40.71); low 40.1 reproduces; I-W5e 35.4 reproduces (35.43)
caveats: High 43.9 depends on the I-D4e add-on (S15)

variable: Audit I-W5b to I-W5d tail shares against the pack tail
definition: I-W5b (Pareto top 1% of households), I-W5c and I-W5d (adult top 1% and 10%, 2016-18) against the pack tail
value_or_range: WID 21.3 and 57.1 (2024, adults) against the register 14.4 to 23.0 and 52.4 to 52.5 (2016-18, adults)
caveats: Definitions and years differ; I-W5b is a derived (J) household figure not tested here

variable: Audit I-W4a to I-W4f mobility rows
definition: I-W4a to I-W4c (UK mobility); I-W4d, I-W4e (Norway); I-W4f (intergenerational slope)
source_reference: existing_row_audit.csv; moments.csv AB-02, BF-04; I-W4d to f not re-read
value_or_range: I-W4a/b 80 / 90 reproduce; I-W4c 74 / 77 reproduce; I-W4c central 75.5 is the register midpoint (J)
caveats: I-W4d to I-W4f were not audited against a held file (Norway and Bozio-type sources are not held as tables)
proposed_ruling: supports I-W4a to c; I-W4d to f not audited
open_question_or_data_request: Held copies of the Norway and intergenerational papers if an audit is wanted

definition: T_WDT: WDT paid by the household, net of refund
